hints: Because time was recorded to the nearest second, determine the upper boundary for each class interval (e.g. 3 to 5 has upper boundary 5.5).
Plot each cumulative frequency at its upper class boundary: (5.5, 10), (8.5, 25), (11.5, 42), (16.5, 46), (25.5, 48) and connect them.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Identify the true class boundaries.
Because acceleration time was measured to the nearest whole second, the discrete interval labels represent continuous intervals:
- $3 - 5$ corresponds to $[2.5, 5.5)$ with upper boundary $5.5$
- $6 - 8$ corresponds to $[5.5, 8.5)$ with upper boundary $8.5$
- $9 - 11$ corresponds to $[8.5, 11.5)$ with upper boundary $11.5$
- $12 - 16$ corresponds to $[11.5, 16.5)$ with upper boundary $16.5$
- $17 - 25$ corresponds to $[16.5, 25.5)$ with upper boundary $25.5$

Step 2: Compute the cumulative frequencies:
- At $t = 2.5$: $\text{CF} = 0$
- At $t = 5.5$: $\text{CF} = 10$
- At $t = 8.5$: $\text{CF} = 10 + 15 = 25$
- At $t = 11.5$: $\text{CF} = 25 + 17 = 42$
- At $t = 16.5$: $\text{CF} = 42 + 4 = 46$
- At $t = 25.5$: $\text{CF} = 46 + 2 = 48$

Step 3: Plot the points accurately at these upper boundaries:
$$(2.5, 0), \quad (5.5, 10), \quad (8.5, 25), \quad (11.5, 42), \quad (16.5, 46), \quad (25.5, 48)$$
Step 4: Join these points with a smooth, monotonic increasing curve or a cumulative frequency polygon.

hints: Notice that 35 cars took MORE than $t$ seconds.
Calculate the number of cars that took $t$ seconds or less: $48 - 35 = 13$.
Find 13 on the vertical cumulative frequency axis and read the corresponding time $t$ from your graph.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Interpret the given condition.
We are told that $35$ cars took more than $t$ seconds to accelerate.
Because cumulative frequency represents the number of cars taking less than or equal to a given time, the cumulative frequency at time $t$ is:
$$\text{CF}(t) = 48 - 35 = 13$$

Step 2: Read $t$ from the graph.
Locate $13$ on the vertical cumulative frequency axis, trace horizontally to intersect the cumulative frequency curve, and project vertically down to the horizontal time axis:
$$t \approx 6.5\text{ seconds}$$
Any value in the range $6.0 \le t \le 7.0\text{ seconds}$ is fully accepted.
